data.name: Ragupathi
data.gender_notes: Ragupathi is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ragupathi is a name derived from the Sanskrit language, which means 'Lord Vishnu'. In Hinduism, Vishnu is one of the principal deities, known as the preserver of the universe. This name is often used as a term of reverence and is believed to bring blessings of loyalty, protection, and strength. The name Ragupathi carries the meaning “Lord Vishnu” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Tamil, Sanskrit. Parents who choose Ragupathi usually hope their child will grow to embody lord vishnu and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Ragupathi is a divine name that represents the supreme power and protection of Lord Vishnu. It is a powerful name that is believed to bring blessings of loyalty, protection, and strength.
data.etymology: Ragupathi belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord Vishnu.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ragupathi total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

historical_references.reference: Ragupathi, also known as Raghavendra Swami, was a renowned 16th-century Hindu philosopher and theologian from South India. He is widely revered for his contributions to the Dvaita philosophy, a major school of Hinduism. Ragupathi lived during the Vijayanagara Empire period, and is believed to have been born in 1535 in the village of Sangama Taluk in Karnataka.
historical_references.context: Renaissance of Hinduism and Dvaita philosophy

historical_references.reference: Ragupathi, also known as Thirupathi or Raghavendra, was the 12th Tirumala Tirupati Devaswom (TTD) pontiff in the lineage of Bhagavad Ramanuja. He is believed to have lived during the 13th-14th centuries and is associated with the Tirumala Venkadeswara Temple in Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh, India. Ragupathi is revered for his devotion to Lord Venkateswara and his contributions to the temple's administration.
historical_references.context: Tirumala Venkateswara Temple and the TTD lineage

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Ragupathi' is a revered name in Hinduism, derived from the Sanskrit words 'Raga' meaning melody or mood and 'Pathi' meaning master or lord. In modern context, this name is widely used in various forms across three major platforms: Devotional music, Hinduism in Diaspora, and Yoga and mindfulness. On Spotify, there are several playlists dedicated to devotional music featuring 'Ragupathi' in the name. These playlists offer a collection of bhajans, kirtans, and shlokas dedicated to Lord Ragupathi. On YouTube, there are numerous channels streaming live devotional programs, lectures, and rituals related to Lord Ragupathi. Additionally, there is a growing trend of using 'Ragupathi' in the context of Yoga and mindfulness. Meditation apps, like Headspace and Calm, offer guided meditation sessions with music and mantras dedicated to Lord Ragupathi. In the Hindu diaspora, the name 'Ragupathi' has gained popularity as a symbol of faith and devotion, especially among the Indian community living abroad. These platforms have made it possible for people to connect with their spirituality and tradition, regardless of their physical location.
